title: General English: A1 to C2
description: One path from A1 to C2: two units per level, each with a short reading, its words and practice on one grammar point. Runs from the verb to be at A1 to register and idiom at C2. Written for Bo-ok.

units.title: My Name Is Leyla
units.goal: A1 · The verb to be: I am, you are, he / she / it is.

blocks.text: Read
Hello! My name is Leyla. I am twenty years old. I am from Izmir, in Turkey. I am a student.
My brother is Can. He is sixteen. He is a student too. My parents are teachers. Our house is small, but it is very nice.
My best friend is Sara. She is from Jordan. We are in the same English class. Our teacher is Mr Brown. He is from Canada. He is friendly and funny.
Words

items.example: My name is Omar.
I am a student.
My brother is ten.
My parents are at home.
Our teacher is from Canada.
The people here are friendly.
The room is small.

blocks.text: Grammar: am, is, are
I am · you are · he is · she is · it is · we are · they are. Short forms: I'm, you're, he's, she's, it's, we're, they're. Not: isn't, aren't, I'm not.

blocks.prompt: I ___ a student.

why.tr: "I" ile her zaman "am" kullanılır: I am (kısa: I'm).
why.ar: مع I نستخدم دائمًا am: I am (والمختصر I'm).
why.en: With "I" we always use "am".

blocks.example: I am from Turkey.

blocks.prompt: My parents ___ teachers.

why.tr: "My parents" çoğul (iki kişi) = they. "they" ile "are" kullanılır.
why.ar: My parents جمع (شخصان) أي they، ومع they نستخدم are.
why.en: "My parents" = they, so "are".

blocks.example: My friends are from Jordan.

blocks.prompt: Sara ___ from Jordan.

why.tr: "Sara" tek bir kişi = she. "he / she / it" ile "is" kullanılır.
why.ar: Sara شخص واحد أي she، ومع he وshe وit نستخدم is.
why.en: "Sara" = she, so "is".

blocks.example: My mother is a doctor.

blocks.prompt: We ___ in the same class.

why.tr: "we" ile "are" kullanılır: we are (kısa: we're).
why.ar: مع we نستخدم are: we are (والمختصر we're).
why.en: With "we" we use "are".

blocks.example: We are good friends.

blocks.prompt: How old ___ your brother?

why.tr: "your brother" = he. Soru cümlesinde "is" öznenin önüne geçer: How old is he?
why.ar: your brother أي he، وفي السؤال تتقدّم is على الفاعل: How old is he?
why.en: "Your brother" = he. In questions, "is" comes before the subject.

blocks.example: How old is your sister?

blocks.prompt: Our house ___ big. It is small.

why.tr: Olumsuz: is not = isn't. "house" tekil (it), bu yüzden "aren't" değil "isn't". Sadece "not" yetmez; fiil gerekir.
why.ar: النفي: is not = isn't. البيت مفرد (it)، فنقول isn't لا aren't. ولا تكفي not وحدها، نحتاج إلى الفعل.
why.en: Negative of "is" is "isn't". "Not" alone needs a verb.

blocks.example: The test isn't difficult.

blocks.prompt: ___ you from Turkey?

why.tr: "you" ile "are" kullanılır. Soru için "are" başa gelir: Are you...? "Do" burada yanlış, çünkü cümlede başka fiil yok.
why.ar: مع you نستخدم are، وفي السؤال نضعها أولًا: Are you...? أما Do فخطأ هنا لأنه لا يوجد فعل آخر.
why.en: With "you", use "are"; put it first to make a question.

blocks.example: Are you a teacher?

blocks.prompt: Mr Brown ___ friendly and funny.

why.tr: "Mr Brown" tek bir kişi = he → is.
why.ar: Mr Brown شخص واحد أي he ← is.
why.en: "Mr Brown" = he → is.

blocks.example: My teacher is very kind.

units.title: Omar's Day
units.goal: A1 · Present simple: he works, he doesn't work, does he work?

blocks.text: Read
Omar lives in Amman. He works in a bank. Every day, he gets up at seven o'clock. He has tea and bread for breakfast. He goes to work by bus.
He starts work at nine and finishes at five. In the evening, he cooks dinner with his wife, Huda. They eat at eight. Omar doesn't watch TV. He reads a book or calls his mother.
On Fridays, he doesn't work. He plays football with his friends in the park.
Words

items.example: I get up at seven.
I have eggs for breakfast.
She goes to school by bus.
The film starts at eight.
School finishes at three.
We eat dinner in the evening.
I call my sister every day.

blocks.text: Grammar: present simple
We use the present simple for habits and things that are always true. I / you / we / they work. He / she / it works (add -s). Negative: don't / doesn't + verb. Question: Do / Does … + verb?

blocks.prompt: Omar ___ in a bank.

why.tr: "Omar" = he. Geniş zamanda he / she / it ile fiile -s eklenir: he works.
why.ar: Omar أي he، وفي المضارع البسيط نضيف -s للفعل مع he وshe وit: he works.
why.en: He / she / it: add -s to the verb.

blocks.example: My father works in a hospital.

blocks.prompt: He ___ to work by bus. (go)

why.tr: "go" fiili -o ile bitiyor; he / she / it ile -es alır: goes. Aynı şekilde: do → does, watch → watches.
why.ar: الفعل go ينتهي بـ -o، فنضيف -es مع he: goes. ومثله do ← does وwatch ← watches.
why.en: Verbs ending in -o take -es: go → goes.

blocks.example: She goes to the gym on Mondays.

blocks.prompt: They ___ dinner at eight.

why.tr: "they" ile fiil yalın kalır, -s almaz: they eat.
why.ar: مع they يبقى الفعل مجردًا بلا -s: they eat.
why.en: With "they", no -s: they eat.

blocks.example: We eat lunch at one o'clock.

blocks.prompt: Omar ___ watch TV.

why.tr: He / she / it ile olumsuz "doesn't + yalın fiil". "isn't" "be" fiili içindir: He isn't tired.
why.ar: النفي مع he وshe وit هو doesn't + فعل مجرد. أما isn't فهي للفعل be: He isn't tired.
why.en: Negative with he/she/it: doesn't + base verb.

blocks.example: My sister doesn't like coffee.

blocks.prompt: ___ Omar work on Fridays? No, he doesn't.

why.tr: He / she / it ile soru: "Does + özne + yalın fiil?" Fiil -s almaz: Does he work? (Does he works değil.)
why.ar: السؤال مع he وshe وit: Does + فاعل + فعل مجرد؟ ولا يأخذ الفعل -s: Does he work?
why.en: Questions with he/she/it: Does + subject + base verb.

blocks.example: Does your brother play football?

blocks.prompt: Huda ___ tea every morning. (have)

why.tr: "have" düzensizdir: he / she / it ile "has" olur.
why.ar: الفعل have شاذّ، ومع he وshe وit يصبح has.
why.en: "Have" becomes "has" with he/she/it.

blocks.example: He has a big family.

blocks.prompt: I ___ like coffee.

why.tr: I / you / we / they ile olumsuz "don't + fiil". "am not" "be" ile kullanılır: I am not tired.
why.ar: النفي مع I وyou وwe وthey هو don't + فعل. أما am not فمع be: I am not tired.
why.en: With I/you/we/they: don't + verb.

blocks.example: We don't live in the city.

blocks.prompt: He ___ a film on Saturdays. (watch)

why.tr: -ch, -sh, -s, -x ile biten fiiller he / she / it ile -es alır: watch → watches, wash → washes.
why.ar: الأفعال المنتهية بـ -ch و-sh و-s و-x تأخذ -es مع he: watch ← watches.
why.en: Verbs ending in -ch, -sh, -s, -x take -es.

blocks.example: She washes the dishes after dinner.

units.title: A Week by the Sea
units.goal: A2 · Past simple: regular and irregular verbs, didn't and did … ?

blocks.text: Read

Last summer, my family and I went to the sea for a week. We stayed in a small hotel near the beach. On the first day, we swam in the morning and visited an old castle in the afternoon. My little sister found some beautiful shells.

In the evening, we ate fish at a restaurant by the water. The food was delicious, but it was expensive. On the third day, it rained, so we didn't go to the beach. We played cards in the hotel and watched a film.
I really enjoyed the holiday. I didn't want to go home!
Words

items.example: We stayed with my aunt.
The castle is eight hundred years old.
She found a shell on the beach.
The soup was delicious.
The hotel was expensive.
Did you enjoy the film?

blocks.text: Grammar: past simple

We use the past simple for finished actions in the past (last summer, yesterday, in 2010). Regular verbs add -ed: stay → stayed. Many common verbs are irregular: go → went, eat → ate, find → found, swim → swam. Negative: didn't + verb. Question: Did … + verb?

blocks.prompt: We ___ in a small hotel. (stay)

why.tr: "stay" düzenli bir fiil: -ed alır → stayed. Ünlü + y ile biten fiillerde y değişmez: play → played.
why.ar: stay فعل قياسي يأخذ -ed ← stayed. وإذا جاءت y بعد حرف علّة لا تتغيّر: play ← played.
why.en: Regular verb: add -ed. After a vowel, y stays: stayed.

blocks.example: We stayed at home last night.

blocks.prompt: We ___ to the sea last summer. (go)

why.tr: "go" düzensiz: geçmiş hâli "went". "goed" diye bir kelime yok.
why.ar: go فعل شاذّ، وماضيه went. لا توجد كلمة goed.
why.en: "Go" is irregular: went.

blocks.example: She went to Paris in 2019.

blocks.prompt: My sister ___ some shells.

why.tr: "find" düzensiz: find → found. Dikkat: "founded" ayrı bir fiil olan "found" (kurmak) fiilinin geçmişidir.
why.ar: find فعل شاذّ: find ← found. انتبه: founded ماضي فعل آخر هو found بمعنى "أسّس".
why.en: find → found. ("Founded" means "started a company or city".)

blocks.example: I found my keys under the sofa.

blocks.prompt: We ___ go to the beach on the third day.

why.tr: Geçmişte olumsuz: "didn't + yalın fiil". "weren't" "be" fiilinin olumsuzudur: We weren't happy.
why.ar: النفي في الماضي: didn't + فعل مجرد. أما weren't فنفي be: We weren't happy.
why.en: Past negative: didn't + base verb.

blocks.example: I didn't see him yesterday.

blocks.prompt: Did you ___ the castle?

why.tr: "Did" geçmişi zaten gösteriyor; ardından fiil yalın gelir: Did you visit? (Did you visited değil.)
why.ar: Did تدل على الماضي، فيأتي بعدها الفعل مجردًا: Did you visit? وليس visited.
why.en: After "did", use the base verb.

blocks.example: Did you call your mother?

blocks.prompt: The food ___ delicious. (be)

why.tr: "be" fiilinin geçmişi: I / he / she / it → was; you / we / they → were. "The food" = it → was.
why.ar: ماضي be: مع I وhe وshe وit ← was، ومع you وwe وthey ← were. الطعام = it ← was.
why.en: "The food" = it → was.

blocks.example: The weather was lovely.

blocks.prompt: In the evening, we ___ fish. (eat)

why.tr: "eat" düzensiz: eat → ate → eaten. Geçmiş zaman için "ate".
why.ar: eat فعل شاذّ: eat ← ate ← eaten. للماضي البسيط نستخدم ate.
why.en: eat → ate.

blocks.example: We ate pizza on Saturday.

blocks.prompt: ___ it rain on the third day? Yes, it did.

why.tr: Cevap "Yes, it did" olduğuna göre soru "Did" ile kurulur. "rain" bir fiil, bu yüzden "Was" değil.
why.ar: الجواب "Yes, it did"، فالسؤال يبدأ بـ Did. وrain فعل، لذا لا نستخدم Was.
why.en: The short answer "Yes, it did" shows the question uses "did".

blocks.example: Did it snow last winter?

blocks.prompt: They ___ English together yesterday. (study)

why.tr: Ünsüz + y ile biten fiillerde y → i olur ve -ed eklenir: study → studied, carry → carried.
why.ar: إذا انتهى الفعل بـ y بعد حرف ساكن تتحوّل y إلى i ثم نضيف -ed: study ← studied.
why.en: Consonant + y: change y to i and add -ed.

blocks.example: She carried the bags to the car.

units.title: Village or City?
units.goal: A2 · Comparatives and superlatives: quieter than, more exciting, the best.

blocks.text: Read
My grandparents live in a village. I live in a city. The village is smaller and quieter than the city, and the air is cleaner. Life there is slower, and people have more time to talk.

But the city is more exciting. There are more shops, cinemas and cafés, and the buses are faster. In my opinion, the best thing about the village is the food: my grandmother's bread is better than any bread in the city!
The worst thing is the internet. I think it is the slowest internet in the world.
Words

items.example: The village has one shop.
The library is very quiet.
The air is clean in the mountains.
The match was exciting.
The old computer is slow.
In my opinion, summer is the best season.

blocks.text: Grammar: comparing

Short adjectives: small → smaller → the smallest. Long adjectives: exciting → more exciting → the most exciting. Spelling: big → bigger, easy → easier. Irregular: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst. Use "than" to compare two things.

blocks.prompt: The village is ___ than the city.

why.tr: "quiet" kısa bir sıfat: -er eklenir → quieter. "than" varsa karşılaştırma (comparative) gerekir, superlative değil.
why.ar: quiet صفة قصيرة نضيف لها -er ← quieter. ووجود than يعني المقارنة لا التفضيل المطلق.
why.en: Short adjective + -er before "than".

blocks.example: My street is quieter than yours.

blocks.prompt: The city is ___ exciting than the village.

why.tr: "exciting" uzun bir sıfat (üç hece): "more + sıfat" ile karşılaştırılır. "excitinger" denmez.
why.ar: exciting صفة طويلة (ثلاثة مقاطع)، فنقول more exciting. لا نقول excitinger.
why.en: Long adjectives use "more".

blocks.example: This book is more interesting than the film.

blocks.prompt: My grandmother's bread is ___ than any bread in the city.

why.tr: "good" düzensiz: good → better → the best. "gooder" ve "more good" yanlış.
why.ar: good صفة شاذّة: good ← better ← the best. لا نقول gooder ولا more good.
why.en: good → better → the best.

blocks.example: Your English is better than mine.

blocks.prompt: I think it is the ___ internet in the world. (slow)

why.tr: "the" + "in the world" en üstünlük (superlative) gösterir: the + sıfat + -est → the slowest.
why.ar: وجود the وin the world يدل على صيغة التفضيل العليا: the + صفة + -est ← the slowest.
why.en: "The … in the world" needs the superlative: the slowest.

blocks.example: This is the oldest building in the city.

blocks.prompt: Today is the ___ day of the year.

why.tr: Tek heceli, ünlü + ünsüz ile biten sıfatlarda son harf ikilenir: hot → hotter → the hottest; big → bigger.
why.ar: الصفات ذات المقطع الواحد المنتهية بحرف علّة + ساكن يتضاعف حرفها الأخير: hot ← hotter ← the hottest.
why.en: One vowel + one consonant: double it: hot → the hottest.

blocks.example: August is the hottest month here.

blocks.prompt: The city is ___ than the village. (big)

why.tr: big → bigger (son harf g ikilenir). "than" olduğu için comparative.
why.ar: big ← bigger (يتضاعف حرف g)، ونستخدم المقارنة لوجود than.
why.en: big → bigger (double the g).

blocks.example: Istanbul is bigger than Ankara.

blocks.prompt: My bag is ___ than yours.

why.tr: Ünsüz + y ile biten sıfatlarda y → i olur: heavy → heavier, easy → easier, happy → happier.
why.ar: إذا انتهت الصفة بـ y بعد حرف ساكن تتحوّل y إلى i: heavy ← heavier وeasy ← easier.
why.en: Consonant + y: change to -ier.

blocks.example: The second test was easier than the first.

blocks.prompt: The ___ thing about the city is the traffic.

why.tr: "bad" düzensiz: bad → worse → the worst. "the" olduğu için superlative: the worst.
why.ar: bad صفة شاذّة: bad ← worse ← the worst. ومع the نستخدم صيغة التفضيل العليا: the worst.
why.en: bad → worse → the worst.

blocks.example: That was the worst film I have ever seen.

units.title: A New Job
units.goal: B1 · Present perfect or past simple: I've lived here for… / I moved in 2020.

blocks.text: Read

Dear Sam, I'm sorry I haven't written for so long. A lot has happened since my last email! I left my old job in March, and I started a new one at a travel company in April. I've been here for six months now, and I've already learned a lot.

Last month I went to Antalya for a conference — my first business trip! I've never travelled for work before, so it was exciting. My new colleagues are friendly. I've made two good friends, Elif and Karim. We had dinner together last Friday.
Have you found a flat yet? Write soon! Love, Mina
Words

items.example: My colleagues are very helpful.
She spoke at a conference in Berlin.
He is away on a business trip.
I've already eaten, thanks.
Have you finished yet?
I've lived here since 2019.

blocks.text: Grammar: present perfect or past simple?

Past simple = a finished time: yesterday, last month, in March, ago. Present perfect (have / has + past participle) = no finished time, or up to now: ever, never, already, yet, for, since. Compare: "I went to Antalya last month." / "I've been to Antalya twice."

blocks.prompt: I ___ my old job in March.

why.tr: "in March" bitmiş bir zaman, bu yüzden past simple: left. Present perfect bitmiş zaman ifadeleriyle (in March, yesterday, ago) kullanılmaz.
why.ar: "in March" زمن منتهٍ، فنستخدم الماضي البسيط: left. لا نستخدم المضارع التام مع أزمنة منتهية مثل in March وyesterday وago.
why.en: "In March" is a finished time → past simple.

blocks.example: She left school in 2015.

blocks.prompt: I ___ here for six months now.

why.tr: Geçmişte başlayıp hâlâ devam eden durum + "for six months" → present perfect: have been. Türkçede "altı aydır buradayım" dediğimiz için "am" kullanmak yaygın bir hatadır.
why.ar: حالة بدأت في الماضي وما زالت مستمرة + for six months ← المضارع التام: have been. ومن الأخطاء الشائعة قول I am here for six months.
why.en: Started in the past and still true + "for" → present perfect.

blocks.example: We have known each other for ten years.

blocks.prompt: Which question is correct?
options: Have you ever been to Japan?
Are you ever been to Japan?
Have you ever went to Japan?
Do you ever been to Japan?

why.tr: Present perfect: have / has + V3 (past participle). "go" fiilinin V3'ü "gone", ama deneyim için "been to" kullanılır. "went" V2'dir, "have" ile gelmez.
why.ar: المضارع التام: have/has + التصريف الثالث. ولسؤال التجربة نستخدم been to. أما went فهي التصريف الثاني ولا تأتي بعد have.
why.en: Present perfect = have + past participle; for experience we say "been to".

blocks.example: Have you ever been to Egypt?

blocks.prompt: We ___ dinner together last Friday. (have)

why.tr: "last Friday" bitmiş zaman → past simple. "have" fiilinin geçmişi "had".
why.ar: "last Friday" زمن منتهٍ ← الماضي البسيط، وماضي have هو had.
why.en: "Last Friday" → past simple: had.

blocks.example: We had a party last weekend.

blocks.prompt: I've ___ two good friends. (make)

why.tr: "I've" = I have → ardından V3 gelir. make → made → made.
why.ar: I've = I have، ويأتي بعدها التصريف الثالث: make ← made ← made.
why.en: After "have", the past participle: made.

blocks.example: She has made a cake for your birthday.

blocks.prompt: Have you found a flat ___?

why.tr: "yet" soru ve olumsuz cümlelerde cümle sonunda kullanılır: Have you finished yet? / I haven't finished yet. "already" genellikle olumlu cümlededir; "ago" past simple ile gelir.
why.ar: yet تُستخدم في السؤال والنفي في آخر الجملة: Have you finished yet? أما already فغالبًا في الإثبات، وago مع الماضي البسيط.
why.en: "Yet" goes at the end of questions and negatives.

blocks.example: I haven't read the email yet.

blocks.prompt: I ___ to Antalya last month.

why.tr: "last month" bitmiş zaman → past simple: went. Zaman belli değilse present perfect olurdu: I've been to Antalya.
why.ar: "last month" زمن منتهٍ ← الماضي البسيط: went. لو لم يُذكر الزمن لقلنا I've been to Antalya.
why.en: "Last month" → past simple.

blocks.example: They went to Cairo two years ago.

blocks.prompt: She has lived here ___ 2020.

why.tr: "since" + başlangıç noktası (2020, Monday, I was a child). "for" + süre (three years, a week).
why.ar: since + نقطة البداية (2020، يوم الاثنين). وfor + المدة (ثلاث سنوات، أسبوع).
why.en: since + a point in time; for + a period.

blocks.example: I have worked here since January.

blocks.prompt: I ___ for work before. (never / travel)

why.tr: Hayat boyu deneyim, zaman yok → present perfect: have + never + V3. İngiliz İngilizcesinde "travelled", Amerikan İngilizcesinde "traveled".
why.ar: تجربة في الحياة بلا زمن محدد ← المضارع التام: have + never + التصريف الثالث. travelled في البريطانية وtraveled في الأمريكية.
why.en: Life experience → have never + past participle.

blocks.example: I have never seen snow.

units.title: If the Weather Is Good…
units.goal: B1 · First conditional: if + present, will + verb; unless.

blocks.text: Read
Kemal and Rania are planning a trip to the mountains on Saturday. "If the weather is good, we'll walk to the lake," says Kemal. "But if it rains, we'll visit the museum in the town instead."
Rania is thinking about the cost. "If we take the train, it'll be cheaper than driving," she says. "And we won't need to find a parking space."

Kemal agrees, but he has one condition. "We'll miss the early train unless we leave home by seven. If you're late, I'll go without you!" Rania laughs. "Don't worry. I'll set two alarms if it makes you happy."
Words

items.example: We are planning a holiday.
There was no tea, so I had coffee instead.
The cost of the trip is low.
I'll help you on one condition.
We'll be late unless we hurry.
Hurry or you'll miss the bus.
I set an alarm for six.

blocks.text: Grammar: first conditional

We use the first conditional for a real possibility in the future: If + present simple, will + verb. "If it rains, we'll stay at home." Do not use "will" after "if". "Unless" means "if … not": "unless we leave" = "if we don't leave".

blocks.prompt: If it ___, we'll visit the museum.

why.tr: "if" kısmında gelecekten söz etsek de present simple kullanılır: If it rains. "If it will rain" yanlış. Türkçedeki "yağarsa" gibi düşün.
why.ar: في جملة if نستخدم المضارع البسيط حتى لو كان الحديث عن المستقبل: If it rains. لا نقول If it will rain.
why.en: After "if", use the present simple, not "will".

blocks.example: If it snows, the schools will close.

blocks.prompt: If we take the train, it ___ cheaper.

why.tr: Sonuç kısmı: will + yalın fiil. "would be" ikinci tip koşul içindir (hayalî durum).
why.ar: جملة النتيجة: will + فعل مجرد. أما would be فللشرط من النوع الثاني (الخيالي).
why.en: Result clause: will + base verb.

blocks.example: If you study, you will pass.

blocks.prompt: If you ___ late, I'll go without you. (be)

why.tr: "if" sonrası present simple: you are. "If you will be late" yanlış.
why.ar: بعد if نستخدم المضارع البسيط: you are. لا نقول If you will be late.
why.en: Present simple after "if": you are.

blocks.example: If you are tired, we'll go home.

blocks.prompt: We ___ to find a parking space if we take the train. (not need)

why.tr: Sonuç kısmında olumsuz: won't (= will not) + yalın fiil.
why.ar: النفي في جملة النتيجة: won't (= will not) + فعل مجرد.
why.en: Negative result: won't + base verb.

blocks.example: If we leave now, we won't be late.

blocks.prompt: We'll miss the train ___ we leave by seven.

why.tr: "unless" = "if ... not": Yedide çıkMAZSAK treni kaçırırız. "if" ile anlam ters olur (yedide çıkarsak kaçırırız).
why.ar: unless = if ... not: سيفوتنا القطار ما لم نخرج قبل السابعة. ومع if يصبح المعنى معكوسًا.
why.en: "Unless" = if not: unless we leave = if we don't leave.

blocks.example: You won't get better unless you rest.

blocks.prompt: Unless you hurry, you ___ the bus.

why.tr: "unless" de birinci koşul gibi kullanılır: unless + present, will + fiil.
why.ar: unless تعمل مثل الشرط الأول: unless + مضارع، will + فعل.
why.en: Unless + present, will + verb.

blocks.example: Unless it stops raining, we will stay inside.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: If I will see her, I will tell her.
If I see her, I'll tell her.
If I see her, I tell her tomorrow.
If I saw her, I will tell her.

why.tr: Doğru yapı: If + present, will + fiil. A'da "if" sonrası "will" var; C'de "tomorrow" olmasına rağmen "will" yok; D'de zamanlar karışmış.
why.ar: التركيب الصحيح: If + مضارع، will + فعل. في A جاءت will بعد if، وفي C لا توجد will رغم tomorrow، وفي D الأزمنة مختلطة.
why.en: If + present, will + verb.

blocks.example: If I see Karim, I'll give him your message.

blocks.prompt: What will you do if the shop ___ early? (close)

why.tr: "if" sonrası present simple ve "the shop" = it → closes.
why.ar: بعد if المضارع البسيط، وthe shop أي it ← closes.
why.en: Present simple after "if"; it → closes.

blocks.example: If the bank closes early, I'll go tomorrow.

units.title: From Bean to Bar
units.goal: B2 · The passive: is made, are dried, has been enjoyed, will be opened.

blocks.text: Read

Chocolate begins life as the seed of the cacao tree, which is grown in hot, wet regions near the equator. Today, most of the world's cacao is produced in West Africa, especially in Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana. The pods are cut from the trees by hand, and the beans inside are removed. The beans are then left to ferment for several days, which develops their flavour, before they are dried in the sun.

After they have been dried, the beans are packed into sacks and shipped to factories. There, they are roasted and their shells are removed. The inside of the bean is ground into a thick paste. Sugar, and sometimes milk, is added, and the mixture is mixed and warmed for hours to make it smooth. Finally, the chocolate is cooled carefully, poured into moulds and wrapped.
Chocolate has been enjoyed for thousands of years, but for most of that time it was drunk, not eaten. Solid bars were only made from the nineteenth century.
Words

items.example: Plant the seeds in spring.
Singapore is close to the equator.
Grapes are fermented to make vinegar.
Coffee beans are roasted before they are ground.
The wheat is ground into flour.
Pour the mixture into a mould.
The gifts were wrapped in paper.

blocks.text: Grammar: the passive

Form: be + past participle. Present: is / are made. Past: was / were made. Present perfect: has / have been made. Future: will be made. We use the passive when the action matters more than who does it — very common in descriptions of processes and in IELTS Writing Task 1. Add "by …" only if the doer is important.

blocks.prompt: Most of the world's cacao ___ in West Africa.

why.tr: Kakao kendisi üretmiyor; biri onu üretiyor → edilgen: is + V3. Tek başına "produced" (be olmadan) cümleyi tamamlamaz.
why.ar: الكاكاو لا يُنتج نفسه بل يُنتَج، فنستخدم المبني للمجهول: is + التصريف الثالث. وكلمة produced وحدها بلا be لا تكمل الجملة.
why.en: Cacao does not produce anything; it is produced → be + past participle.

blocks.example: Most of the country's rice is grown in the south.

blocks.prompt: The pods ___ from the trees by hand. (cut)

why.tr: Çoğul özne (the pods) + present passive: are + V3. "cut" fiilinin üç hâli de aynı: cut – cut – cut.
why.ar: فاعل جمع (the pods) + المبني للمجهول في المضارع: are + التصريف الثالث. وتصاريف cut الثلاثة واحدة.
why.en: Plural + present passive: are cut.

blocks.example: The grapes are picked by hand.

blocks.prompt: The beans ___ in the sun. (dry)

why.tr: Present passive: are + V3. dry → dried (ünsüz + y → ied).
why.ar: المبني للمجهول في المضارع: are + التصريف الثالث. dry ← dried.
why.en: are + past participle: are dried.

blocks.example: The clothes are dried outside in summer.

blocks.prompt: After drying, the beans ___ to factories.

why.tr: Fasulyeler kendini göndermiyor; gönderiliyorlar → are shipped. "have shipped" etken yapı olur (onlar bir şey göndermiş).
why.ar: الحبوب لا ترسل نفسها بل تُرسَل ← are shipped. أما have shipped فمبني للمعلوم بمعنى أنها أرسلت شيئًا.
why.en: The beans receive the action → passive.

blocks.example: The parcels are shipped every Monday.

blocks.prompt: Chocolate ___ for thousands of years.

why.tr: "for thousands of years" bugüne kadar süren bir dönem → present perfect; çikolata zevkle yeniyor (edilgen) → has been + V3.
why.ar: "for thousands of years" مدة ممتدة حتى الآن ← المضارع التام، والشوكولاتة يُستمتع بها (مجهول) ← has been + التصريف الثالث.
why.en: Up to now + passive: has been enjoyed.

blocks.example: Tea has been drunk in China for centuries.

blocks.prompt: For most of its history, chocolate ___ drunk, not eaten.

why.tr: Geçmişte edilgen: was / were + V3. "chocolate" tekil → was drunk.
why.ar: المبني للمجهول في الماضي: was/were + التصريف الثالث. الشوكولاتة مفرد ← was drunk.
why.en: Past passive, singular: was drunk.

blocks.example: The castle was built in the twelfth century.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is passive?
options: Sugar is added to the mixture.

why.tr: Edilgen = be + V3 ve özne eylemi yapan değil, eylemden etkilenendir: Sugar IS ADDED. D'de "are adding" be + -ing (sürekli zaman), edilgen değil.
why.ar: المبني للمجهول = be + التصريف الثالث، والفاعل يقع عليه الفعل: Sugar is added. في D نجد are adding وهو زمن مستمر لا مبني للمجهول.
why.en: Passive = be + past participle. "Are adding" is continuous, not passive.

blocks.example: The letters are sorted by machine.

blocks.prompt: A new chocolate factory ___ in the town next year. (open)

why.tr: "next year" gelecek; edilgen gelecek zaman: will be + V3.
why.ar: "next year" مستقبل، والمبني للمجهول في المستقبل: will be + التصريف الثالث.
why.en: Future passive: will be + past participle.

blocks.example: The new bridge will be opened in May.

blocks.prompt: Why does the text use the passive so often?
options: Because the process matters more than who does each step.
Because the passive is always more polite.
Because the writer does not know English well.
Because the active voice cannot be used for food.

why.tr: Süreç anlatırken önemli olan ne yapıldığıdır, kimin yaptığı değil. Bu yüzden IELTS Task 1 süreç sorularında edilgen çok kullanılır.
why.ar: عند وصف عملية يهمّنا ما يحدث لا من يقوم به، ولذلك يكثر المبني للمجهول في أسئلة وصف العمليات في الآيلتس.
why.en: In a process, the action matters more than the doer.

blocks.example: The water is cleaned, tested and then pumped into homes.

units.title: A Missed Flight
units.goal: B2 · Second and third conditionals: if I had…, I would…; if I had known…, I would have…

blocks.text: Read

Two years ago, Deniz missed a flight to Berlin, and it changed his life. "If I hadn't overslept, I would have caught the plane," he says. "And if I had caught it, I would never have met Lina." Lina was waiting for the next flight too, and they started talking in the airport café. Today they run a small design studio together.

Deniz sometimes thinks about how different things could be. "If I still worked in my old office, I would earn more money, but I wouldn't be as happy. Even if I had the chance to go back, I wouldn't change anything."
Lina is more practical. "If he had set an alarm," she laughs, "he would have saved himself a lot of stress that morning."
Words

items.example: I overslept and missed the first lesson.
We caught the plane with five minutes to spare.
They run a small café.
She earns more than her brother.
I'd love the chance to travel.
We need a practical solution.

blocks.text: Grammar: imaginary situations

Second conditional — imaginary now or future: If + past simple, would + verb. "If I had more time, I would learn the guitar." (I don't have time.) Third conditional — imaginary past: If + past perfect, would have + past participle. "If I had left earlier, I wouldn't have missed the plane." (I didn't leave earlier.) With "be", we often use "were": If I were you…

blocks.prompt: If I hadn't overslept, I ___ the plane.

why.tr: Geçmişte gerçekleşmemiş bir durum (üçüncü tip): If + had + V3, would have + V3. Uyuyakaldı ve uçağı kaçırdı; hayal ettiği geçmiş farklı.
why.ar: حالة ماضية لم تحدث (الشرط الثالث): If + had + التصريف الثالث، would have + التصريف الثالث. لقد نام وفاتته الطائرة فعلًا.
why.en: Imaginary past: would have + past participle.

blocks.example: If we had booked earlier, we would have got cheaper tickets.

blocks.prompt: If I ___ more free time, I would learn to play the guitar.

why.tr: Şu anki hayalî durum (ikinci tip): If + past simple, would + fiil. Geçmiş zaman biçimi burada geçmişi değil, gerçek dışılığı gösterir.
why.ar: حالة خيالية في الحاضر (الشرط الثاني): If + ماضٍ بسيط، would + فعل. الماضي هنا لا يدل على زمن ماضٍ بل على أن الأمر غير حقيقي.
why.en: Imaginary present: If + past simple, would + verb.

blocks.example: If I lived near the sea, I would swim every day.

blocks.prompt: If she ___ the answer, she would have told us. (know)

why.tr: Sonuç kısmı "would have told" → üçüncü tip. "if" kısmı past perfect: had + V3 → had known.
why.ar: جملة النتيجة would have told ← الشرط الثالث، فجملة if في الماضي التام: had + التصريف الثالث ← had known.
why.en: Third conditional: if + had + past participle.

blocks.example: If I had known about the party, I would have come.

blocks.prompt: If I were you, I ___ the job. (take)

why.tr: "If I were you" tavsiye vermenin kalıbıdır (ikinci tip): would + yalın fiil.
why.ar: If I were you تعبير لتقديم النصيحة (الشرط الثاني): would + فعل مجرد.
why.en: "If I were you, I would…" gives advice.

blocks.example: If I were you, I would talk to the manager.

blocks.prompt: If I ___ you, I would apologise.

why.tr: İkinci tipte "be" fiili tüm öznelerle "were" olarak kullanılabilir; özellikle "If I were you" kalıbında. "am" gerçek bir durumu anlatır, burada hayalî.
why.ar: في الشرط الثاني نستخدم were مع كل الضمائر، خاصة في If I were you. أما am فتدل على حقيقة، والحالة هنا خيالية.
why.en: Imaginary present with "be": were.

blocks.example: If she were here, she would know what to do.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is about an imaginary situation in the past?
options: If they had left earlier, they wouldn't have missed the train.
If they leave earlier, they won't miss the train.
If they left earlier, they wouldn't miss the train.
When they leave early, they don't miss the train.

why.tr: Sadece A geçmiş hakkında: had left + wouldn't have missed (üçüncü tip). B gerçek gelecek (birinci tip), C hayalî şimdi/gelecek (ikinci tip), D genel alışkanlık.
why.ar: الخيار A وحده عن الماضي: had left + wouldn't have missed (الشرط الثالث). B مستقبل حقيقي، وC خيال في الحاضر، وD عادة عامة.
why.en: Only A uses had + past participle / would have: the past.

blocks.example: If I had studied harder, I would have passed.

blocks.prompt: We ___ if he hadn't missed the flight. (not / meet)

why.tr: "hadn't missed" → üçüncü tip; sonuç: wouldn't have + V3. meet → met.
why.ar: hadn't missed ← الشرط الثالث، والنتيجة: wouldn't have + التصريف الثالث. meet ← met.
why.en: Third conditional result: wouldn't have met.

blocks.example: They wouldn't have met if she hadn't moved to London.

blocks.prompt: If he still worked in his old office, he ___ more money.

why.tr: "still worked" = şu anki hayalî durum (artık orada çalışmıyor) → ikinci tip: would + yalın fiil.
why.ar: still worked تعني حالة خيالية في الحاضر (لم يعد يعمل هناك) ← الشرط الثاني: would + فعل مجرد.
why.en: Imaginary present → would + verb.

blocks.example: If I had a car, I would drive to work.

blocks.prompt: “If I had caught the plane, I would never have met Lina.” What happened?
options: He didn't catch the plane, and he met Lina.
He caught the plane, and he met Lina.
He caught the plane, but he didn't meet Lina.
He didn't catch the plane, and he didn't meet Lina.

why.tr: Üçüncü tip koşul gerçeğin tersini anlatır. "If I had caught" → gerçekte yakalamadı. "would never have met" → gerçekte tanıştı.
why.ar: الشرط الثالث يصف عكس ما حدث: If I had caught ← لم يلحق بها فعلًا، وwould never have met ← تعرّف عليها فعلًا.
why.en: A third conditional describes the opposite of what really happened.

blocks.example: If it hadn't rained, we would have gone out. (It rained; we stayed in.)

units.title: A Lucky Accident
units.goal: C1 · Inversion after negative adverbials: Rarely has…, Not only did…, Only after… did…

blocks.text: Read

In 1928, the Scottish scientist Alexander Fleming returned to his London laboratory after a holiday and noticed something odd. On one of the dishes in which he had been growing bacteria, a mould had appeared, and around it the bacteria had died. Rarely has a moment of untidiness proved so valuable. Not only did the substance produced by the mould, which Fleming called penicillin, kill harmful bacteria, but it also appeared to do little harm to the body.

Yet the story is less simple than it is often told. Fleming struggled to produce the substance in useful amounts, and only after Howard Florey, Ernst Chain and their team at Oxford found a way to purify it, more than a decade later, did penicillin become a practical medicine. Never before had doctors had such an effective weapon against infections that had killed millions.
Little did Fleming imagine, as he cleared his untidy bench that September, how dramatically medicine was about to change. In 1945, he, Florey and Chain shared the Nobel Prize.
Words

items.example: There was mould on the old bread.
Some bacteria are good for us.
The substance was tested on mice.
The water is purified before we drink it.
The cut became an infection.
The old map proved very useful.

blocks.text: Grammar: inversion

After a negative or limiting word at the start of a sentence — never, rarely, seldom, little, not only, only after, not until, hardly, under no circumstances — the auxiliary comes before the subject, as in a question: "Rarely HAS a moment proved so valuable." If there is no auxiliary, use do / does / did: "Not only DID it kill bacteria…" This is formal and emphatic; use it in writing and speeches, not in every sentence.

blocks.prompt: Rarely ___ such a lucky accident.

why.tr: "Rarely" başa gelince soru düzeni gelir: yardımcı fiil + özne + ana fiil → has a scientist had. B normal düzen; inversion yok.
why.ar: عندما تتقدّم Rarely نستخدم ترتيب السؤال: فعل مساعد + فاعل + فعل رئيسي ← has a scientist had. أما B فترتيب عادي بلا قلب.
why.en: After "Rarely": auxiliary + subject + verb.

blocks.example: Rarely have I seen such a beautiful sunset.

blocks.prompt: Not only ___ the substance kill bacteria, but it also did little harm to the body.

why.tr: Cümlede yardımcı fiil yok (killed); past simple'da "did" eklenir ve ana fiil yalın kalır: Not only did it kill...
why.ar: لا يوجد فعل مساعد (killed)، ففي الماضي البسيط نضيف did ويعود الفعل إلى أصله: Not only did it kill...
why.en: No auxiliary in the past simple → add "did" + base verb.

blocks.example: Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.

blocks.prompt: Never before ___ such an effective medicine.

why.tr: "Never before" + yardımcı fiil (had) + özne (doctors) + V3 (had). İki "had" garip görünse de doğru: biri yardımcı fiil, biri "have" fiilinin V3'ü.
why.ar: Never before + فعل مساعد (had) + فاعل (doctors) + تصريف ثالث (had). تكرار had صحيح: الأولى مساعدة والثانية تصريف have الثالث.
why.en: Auxiliary (had) + subject + past participle (had).

blocks.example: Never before had the town seen so many visitors.

blocks.prompt: Only after the Oxford team purified it ___ penicillin become a practical medicine.

why.tr: "Only after + zaman/olay" ile başlayan cümlede inversion ana cümlede olur: ... did penicillin become. İlk kısım (the team purified it) normal düzende kalır.
why.ar: مع Only after يحدث القلب في الجملة الرئيسية: ... did penicillin become، أما الجزء الأول فيبقى بترتيب عادي.
why.en: "Only after X" → inversion in the main clause: did + subject + verb.

blocks.example: Only after the storm had passed did we leave the house.

blocks.prompt: Little ___ that his discovery would win a Nobel Prize.

why.tr: "Little" (= hiç, neredeyse hiç) başta → did + özne + yalın fiil: Little did he know. C'de ana fiil özneden önce; İngilizcede böyle bir düzen yok.
why.ar: Little في البداية بمعنى "لم يكن يعلم أبدًا" ← did + فاعل + فعل مجرد: Little did he know. أما C فترتيب غير موجود في الإنجليزية.
why.en: "Little did he know" = he did not know at all.

blocks.example: Little did we know that the shop would close the next day.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Under no circumstances should you open this door.
Under no circumstances you should open this door.
Under no circumstances you open should this door.
Under no circumstances do you should open this door.

why.tr: Modal fiil (should) varsa onu özneden önce getiririz: should you open. "do" yalnızca yardımcı fiil yokken eklenir.
why.ar: إذا وُجد فعل ناقص (should) نقدّمه على الفاعل: should you open. ولا نضيف do إلا عند غياب الفعل المساعد.
why.en: With a modal, move the modal: should you open.

blocks.example: Under no circumstances should you share your password.

blocks.prompt: Hardly ___ he arrived when the phone rang.

why.tr: "Hardly ... when" = -er -mez: geçmişte bir şey olur olmaz başka bir şey oldu. Yapı: Hardly + had + özne + V3 + when + past simple.
why.ar: Hardly ... when تعني "ما إن ... حتى". التركيب: Hardly + had + فاعل + تصريف ثالث + when + ماضٍ بسيط.
why.en: Hardly + had + subject + past participle + when…

blocks.example: Hardly had we sat down when the film started.

blocks.prompt: Not until 1945 ___ the Nobel Prize.

why.tr: "Not until + zaman" başa gelince inversion: did + özne + yalın fiil. Normal düzen: They didn't receive it until 1945.
why.ar: مع Not until في البداية يحدث القلب: did + فاعل + فعل مجرد. والترتيب العادي: They didn't receive it until 1945.
why.en: "Not until…" → did they receive.

blocks.example: Not until I got home did I realise I had lost my wallet.

blocks.prompt: When does inversion sound most natural?
options: In formal writing and speeches, for emphasis.
In every sentence, to sound advanced.
Only in questions about the past.

why.tr: Inversion resmî ve vurgulu bir yapıdır. IELTS yazısında bir iki kez iyi kullanılırsa etkileyicidir; her cümlede kullanmak yapay durur.
why.ar: القلب تركيب رسمي للتوكيد. استخدامه مرة أو مرتين في مقال الآيلتس مؤثر، أما في كل جملة فيبدو متكلّفًا.
why.en: Inversion is formal and emphatic; use it sparingly.

blocks.example: Not only does the policy save money, but it also reduces pollution.

units.title: What Really Matters
units.goal: C1 · Cleft sentences for emphasis: What makes the difference is…, It was … that…

blocks.text: Read

Many learners believe that the secret of success with a language is talent. In fact, what makes the biggest difference is usually habit. It is not the person who studies for five hours once a month who improves fastest, but the one who does twenty minutes every day. What regular practice does is keep the language active in your memory, so that words and structures come back more easily when you need them.

It was only when I started reading short novels for pleasure that my vocabulary really began to grow. What I had not expected was how quickly I would start to notice the same phrases again and again. All I did was read a few pages each night, and yet, after a year, I could follow conversations that had once seemed far too fast.

The reason many people give up is not that the language is too hard. It is that they expect quick results and lose motivation when progress feels slow. What they need is a routine small enough to keep.
Words

items.example: Reading every night became a habit.
I read novels for pleasure.
Did you notice the new sign?
Don't give up — you're nearly there.
Good teachers increase students' motivation.
A morning routine helps me start the day.

blocks.text: Grammar: cleft sentences

A cleft sentence splits one idea into two parts to put emphasis on one of them. "What" clefts: "Habit makes the difference." → "What makes the difference is habit." "It" clefts: "I started reading in 2020." → "It was in 2020 that I started reading." Also: "All I did was…", "The reason … is that…". These help you stress your main point in speaking and writing.

blocks.prompt: ___ makes the biggest difference is habit.

why.tr: "What" burada "the thing that" (… olan şey) anlamındadır: What makes the difference = The thing that makes the difference. "That" ve "Which" bu konumda tek başına kullanılmaz.
why.ar: What هنا بمعنى the thing that أي "الشيء الذي": What makes the difference is habit. ولا تُستخدم That أو Which وحدهما في هذا الموضع.
why.en: "What" = the thing that.

blocks.example: What I like most about Istanbul is the sea.

blocks.prompt: It ___ only when I started reading that my vocabulary grew.

why.tr: "It" cleft: It + be + vurgulanan kısım + that... Olay geçmişte olduğu için "It was".
why.ar: تركيب It: It + be + الجزء المؤكَّد + that... والحدث في الماضي فنقول It was.
why.en: It-cleft in the past: It was … that …

blocks.example: It was in Cairo that they first met.

blocks.prompt: Which is the correct cleft version of “Regular practice keeps words active”?
options: What regular practice does is keep words active.
What regular practice does is it keeps words active.
It is regular practice what keeps words active.
What does regular practice is keep words active.

why.tr: Bir eylemi vurgulamak için: What + özne + does + is + (to) yalın fiil. B'de fazladan "it" var; C'de "what" yerine "that" olmalı (It is regular practice that...); D'de sıra yanlış.
why.ar: لتأكيد الفعل نقول: What + فاعل + does + is + فعل مجرد. في B ضمير it زائد، وفي C يجب أن تكون that بدل what، وفي D الترتيب خطأ.
why.en: To stress an action: What + subject + does + is + base verb.

blocks.example: What the new law does is protect small shops.

blocks.prompt: All I did ___ read a few pages each night.

why.tr: "All I did" = "The only thing I did" (tekil) ve geçmiş → was. Ardından yalın fiil gelebilir: All I did was read.
why.ar: All I did = The only thing I did (مفرد وفي الماضي) ← was، ويمكن أن يأتي بعدها فعل مجرد: All I did was read.
why.en: "All I did" = the only thing I did → was.

blocks.example: All she wanted was a quiet weekend.

blocks.prompt: It was Karim ___ told me about the course.

why.tr: "It" cleft'te vurgulanan bir kişiyse "who" ya da "that" kullanılır. "what" burada kullanılamaz; "whom" nesne içindir, burada Karim özne (told).
why.ar: في تركيب It إذا كان المؤكَّد شخصًا نستخدم who أو that. لا تصلح what هنا، وwhom للمفعول به بينما Karim فاعل (told).
why.en: Person as subject: It was Karim who (or that)…

blocks.example: It was my sister who found the keys.

blocks.prompt: ___ I need is more time.

why.tr: "What I need" = "The thing that I need". Bu yapı ihtiyacını vurgular: What I need is a holiday!
why.ar: What I need = The thing that I need، وهي تؤكّد ما تحتاجه: What I need is a holiday!
why.en: "What I need is…" stresses the need.

blocks.example: What we need is a better plan.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence puts the emphasis on the place?
options: It was in Cairo that I first heard the song.
I first heard the song in Cairo.
What I first heard in Cairo was the song.
The song was heard by me in Cairo.

why.tr: "It was + in Cairo + that..." yeri öne çıkarır (başka bir yer değil, Kahire'de). C şarkıyı vurgular; B nötr; D gereksiz edilgen.
why.ar: It was + in Cairo + that... يؤكّد المكان (في القاهرة لا في غيرها). C تؤكّد الأغنية، وB محايدة، وD مبني للمجهول بلا داعٍ.
why.en: "It was in Cairo that…" emphasises the place.

blocks.example: It was at university that I learned to cook.

blocks.prompt: The reason many people give up is ___ they expect quick results.

why.tr: Kalıp: "The reason (why) ... is that + cümle". "The reason is because" konuşmada duyulur ama resmî yazıda "that" tercih edilir.
why.ar: التركيب: The reason (why) ... is that + جملة. يُسمع The reason is because في الكلام، لكن that هي المفضّلة في الكتابة الرسمية.
why.en: "The reason … is that …" is the standard written form.

blocks.example: The reason I was late is that the bus broke down.

blocks.prompt: What I had not expected ___ how quickly I would notice the phrases.

why.tr: "What" ile başlayan kısım tekil bir özne gibi davranır ve olay geçmişte → was.
why.ar: الجزء الذي يبدأ بـ What يُعامل كفاعل مفرد، والحدث في الماضي ← was.
why.en: A what-clause is singular: was.

blocks.example: What surprised me was how friendly everyone was.

units.title: Saying the Same Thing Twice
units.goal: C2 · Register: choose formal or informal English to fit the reader and purpose.

blocks.text: Read

Message 1: "Hi Jo, thanks for getting back to me so fast! Sorry, but I can't make the meeting on Thursday — something's come up. Could we push it back to next week? Let me know what works for you. Cheers, Amir"

Message 2: "Dear Ms Johnson, Thank you for your prompt reply. Unfortunately, I am unable to attend the meeting on Thursday owing to an unforeseen commitment. Would it be possible to postpone it until next week? I would be grateful if you could let me know which day would suit you. Kind regards, Amir Haddad"

The two messages carry the same information, but they belong to different registers. The formal version avoids contractions, phrasal verbs such as "push back" and "come up", and friendly openings such as "Hi". Instead, it prefers longer words, many of Latin origin — "postpone", "unforeseen", "attend" — and indirect requests: "I would be grateful if…". Neither is better in itself. A formal email to a close friend sounds cold; an informal one to a new client can sound careless. Skilled writers choose the register that fits the reader and the purpose.
Words

items.example: The essay's register is too informal.
Thank you for your prompt reply.
The delay was due to unforeseen problems.
The match was postponed because of rain.
Over a hundred people attended the talk.
I have a family commitment on Sunday.
Does Monday suit you?

blocks.text: Grammar and style: register

Formal English tends to use single verbs instead of phrasal verbs (postpone, not put off), no contractions (I am, not I'm), indirect requests (Would it be possible…? I would be grateful if…), and less personal openings and closings (Dear…, Kind regards). Informal English is shorter, more direct and more personal. In IELTS, Writing Task 2 needs a formal or neutral register; Task 1 letters (General Training) may be formal, semi-formal or informal depending on the reader.

blocks.prompt: Which is the formal equivalent of “push back” (a meeting)?

why.tr: "push back / put off" = ertelemek → resmî karşılığı "postpone". "cancel" iptal etmek (anlam farklı), "bring forward" öne almak (zıt anlam).
why.ar: push back أو put off بمعنى يؤجّل، ومقابلها الرسمي postpone. أما cancel فتعني يلغي، وbring forward تعني يقدّم الموعد (عكس المعنى).
why.en: push back = postpone. Cancel and bring forward mean different things.

blocks.example: We have decided to postpone the launch until June.

blocks.prompt: Which is the formal equivalent of “get in touch with”?

why.tr: "get in touch with" phrasal bir ifade; resmî tek fiil karşılığı "contact". "hit up" çok gündelik bir argo.
why.ar: get in touch with تعبير غير رسمي، ومقابله الرسمي الفعل contact. أما hit up فعامية جدًا.
why.en: Formal single verb: contact.

blocks.example: Please contact our office if you have any questions.

blocks.prompt: I am ___ to attend the meeting. (formal for “can't”)

why.tr: "I can't" → resmî: "I am unable to + fiil". Kısaltma kullanılmaz.
why.ar: I can't ← في الأسلوب الرسمي: I am unable to + فعل، ودون اختصارات.
why.en: Formal: I am unable to…

blocks.example: We are unable to offer a refund.

blocks.prompt: Which request is the most formal?
options: I would be grateful if you could send the report.
Could you send the report, please?

why.tr: Dolaylılık arttıkça resmîyet artar. "I would be grateful if you could..." en dolaylı ve en resmî; "Send me..." emir kipi, en doğrudan.
why.ar: كلما زادت المباشرة قلّت الرسمية. I would be grateful if you could... هي الأكثر رسمية، وSend me... أمر مباشر.
why.en: The more indirect, the more formal.

blocks.example: I would be grateful if you could confirm the date.

blocks.prompt: Which is best in an IELTS Task 2 essay?

why.tr: "loads of", "tons of", "cash" konuşma dilidir. Akademik yazıda "a great deal of" (sayılamayan) ya da "a large number of" (sayılabilir) tercih edilir.
why.ar: loads of وtons of وcash من لغة الكلام. في الكتابة الأكاديمية نستخدم a great deal of (لغير المعدود) أو a large number of (للمعدود).
why.en: Academic: a great deal of (uncountable), a large number of (countable).

blocks.example: The project requires a great deal of time and effort.

blocks.prompt: We need to ___ the cause of the problem. (one formal verb for “find out”)

why.tr: "find out" phrasal bir fiil. Resmî tek kelimelik karşılıklar: determine, establish, identify, ascertain.
why.ar: find out فعل مركّب غير رسمي، ومقابلاته الرسمية: determine وestablish وidentify وascertain.
why.en: Formal single verbs: determine, establish, identify, ascertain.

blocks.example: The inquiry aims to establish what went wrong.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence would sound too formal in a text message to a close friend?
options: I regret to inform you that I shall be late.
I'll be about ten minutes late.
Sorry, I'm going to be a bit late.

why.tr: "I regret to inform you" ve "shall" resmî mektup dilidir; yakın bir arkadaşa soğuk, hatta komik gelir. Register okuyucuya uymalı.
why.ar: I regret to inform you وshall من لغة الرسائل الرسمية، وتبدو باردة أو مضحكة في رسالة لصديق مقرّب. يجب أن يناسب الأسلوبُ القارئ.
why.en: "I regret to inform you" is for official letters, not friends.

blocks.example: Running late — see you at eight!

blocks.prompt: Which is the formal version of “something's come up”?

why.tr: Resmî sürüm kısaltmasız ve phrasal verb'süz: "come up" → "arise", "something" → "an unforeseen commitment". C ve D hâlâ gündelik.
why.ar: النسخة الرسمية بلا اختصار وبلا أفعال مركّبة: come up ← arise، وsomething ← an unforeseen commitment. أما C وD فلا تزالان عاميّتين.
why.en: come up → arise; something → an unforeseen commitment.

blocks.example: Unfortunately, an unforeseen problem has arisen.

blocks.prompt: “Thanks for your fast reply” → “Thank you for your ___ reply.” (formal)

why.tr: Resmî yazışmada "fast" yerine genellikle "prompt" kullanılır: Thank you for your prompt reply. "swift" de uygundur.
why.ar: في المراسلات الرسمية نستخدم prompt بدل fast: Thank you for your prompt reply. وتصلح swift أيضًا.
why.en: Formal letters use "prompt" (or "swift").

blocks.example: We appreciate your prompt payment.

units.title: Reading Between the Lines
units.goal: C2 · Nuance and idiom: what people mean but do not say.

blocks.text: Read

When Selin joined an international company in London, her English was excellent on paper. What took her by surprise was how much meaning lay beneath the surface of ordinary conversation. When her manager said a proposal was "quite interesting", she assumed he liked it; only later did she realise he was being polite about an idea he had no intention of supporting. When a colleague advised her not to "rock the boat", she understood the words but missed the warning: stop asking awkward questions in meetings.

Over time, she learned to read between the lines. She noticed that "I hear what you're saying" often meant "I disagree", and that "with respect" tended to come just before something rather disrespectful. She also found that idioms are a double-edged sword for learners. Used well, they make speech sound natural; used too often, or slightly wrongly, they sound forced. "It's raining cats and dogs" is perfectly correct, yet to many native speakers it sounds old-fashioned.
The lesson, Selin says, is that understanding English at the highest level is less about knowing more words than about sensing what people mean but do not say.
Words

items.example: The question took me by surprise.
Beneath the surface, she was nervous.
He has no intention of resigning.
She didn't want to rock the boat before the deal was signed.
Read between the lines: they're not happy.
Fame can be a double-edged sword.
His smile looked forced.

blocks.text: Nuance

At C2, the challenge is often not grammar but nuance: two words or phrases can share a meaning but differ in attitude (slim / skinny), strength (annoyed / furious) or formality (kids / children). Idioms add colour, but each has its own setting: many are fine in conversation and wrong in an academic essay.

blocks.prompt: What does “read between the lines” mean?
options: Understand a meaning that is not stated directly.

why.tr: "read between the lines" = açıkça söylenmeyen, ima edilen anlamı anlamak. Türkçede de aynı deyim var: satır aralarını okumak.
why.ar: read between the lines تعني فهم المعنى الضمني غير المصرَّح به، ويقابلها بالعربية "يقرأ ما بين السطور".
why.en: To understand a hidden or implied meaning.

blocks.example: If you read between the lines, the letter is a refusal.

blocks.prompt: If someone tells you not to “rock the boat”, they want you to
options: avoid causing trouble by challenging the situation.
be careful on a boat trip.

why.tr: "rock the boat" = mevcut düzeni sorgulayarak sorun çıkarmak. Genellikle olumsuz cümlelerde: Don't rock the boat.
why.ar: rock the boat تعني إثارة المشاكل بتحدّي الوضع القائم، وتأتي غالبًا في النفي: Don't rock the boat.
why.en: To cause trouble by questioning how things are.

blocks.example: He kept quiet because he didn't want to rock the boat.

blocks.prompt: In British English, a manager who calls your idea “quite interesting” most probably means:
options: He wants to hear more immediately.

why.tr: İngiliz İngilizcesinde "quite" + olumlu sıfat çoğu zaman övgüyü zayıflatır ve kibar bir eksik söyleme (understatement) olabilir. Metinde de yönetici fikri desteklemek istemiyordu.
why.ar: في الإنجليزية البريطانية كثيرًا ما تُضعف quite المديح، وتكون تلطيفًا مهذّبًا. وفي النص لم يكن المدير ينوي دعم الفكرة.
why.en: British "quite interesting" is often polite understatement, as in the text.

blocks.example: "The film was quite good" can mean it was only fairly good.

blocks.prompt: “A double-edged sword” is something that

why.tr: "a double-edged sword" = iki ucu keskin kılıç: hem yararı hem zararı olan şey. Metinde deyimler doğal da gösterebilir, yapay da.
why.ar: a double-edged sword أي سلاح ذو حدّين: له فوائد وأضرار. وفي النص قد تجعل التعابير الكلام طبيعيًا أو متكلّفًا.
why.en: Something with good and bad effects.

blocks.example: Social media is a double-edged sword for young people.

blocks.prompt: The news took everyone ___ surprise.

why.tr: Sabit kalıp: "take someone BY surprise". "with surprise" ya da "in surprise" bu kalıpta kullanılmaz.
why.ar: التعبير الثابت take someone BY surprise، ولا نقول with surprise ولا in surprise هنا.
why.en: The fixed phrase is "take someone by surprise".

blocks.example: The sudden storm took the sailors by surprise.

blocks.prompt: He refused to change his mind. Which word is the most critical?

why.tr: Dördü de "fikrinden dönmeyen" anlamını taşır ama tonları farklı: "determined" ve "persistent" olumlu (azimli), "firm" nötr, "stubborn" olumsuz (inatçı).
why.ar: الكلمات الأربع تعني الثبات على الرأي لكن بنبرات مختلفة: determined وpersistent إيجابيتان (عازم، مثابر)، وfirm محايدة، وstubborn سلبية (عنيد).
why.en: Same idea, different attitude: stubborn is negative.

blocks.example: She is determined; her brother is just stubborn.

blocks.prompt: Which word would usually be heard as a compliment?

why.tr: Hepsi "zayıf" demek, ama "slim" olumlu (ince, alımlı); "skinny", "bony" ve "scrawny" eleştirel ya da olumsuz.
why.ar: كلها تعني نحيفًا، لكن slim إيجابية (رشيق)، أما skinny وbony وscrawny فتحمل انتقادًا.
why.en: All mean thin, but only "slim" is positive.

blocks.example: You look slim and healthy.

blocks.prompt: Which sentence is best in an academic essay?
options: This policy has both advantages and disadvantages.
This policy is a mixed bag, to be honest.
At the end of the day, this policy is swings and roundabouts.
This policy is a bit of a curate's egg.

why.tr: "a mixed bag", "at the end of the day", "swings and roundabouts" konuşma diline ait deyimlerdir; akademik yazıda açık ve nötr bir ifade tercih edilir.
why.ar: a mixed bag وat the end of the day وswings and roundabouts تعابير من لغة الكلام، والكتابة الأكاديمية تفضّل العبارة الواضحة المحايدة.
why.en: Academic writing prefers plain, neutral wording over idioms.

blocks.example: The proposal has both strengths and weaknesses.

blocks.prompt: I'm afraid we're not on the same ___ about this project.

why.tr: "be on the same page" = aynı fikirde olmak, aynı şekilde anlamak. İş yerinde çok yaygın, gündelik-nötr bir deyim.
why.ar: be on the same page تعني أن نتّفق ونفهم الأمر بالطريقة نفسها، وهو تعبير شائع في بيئة العمل.
why.en: "Be on the same page" = agree / understand in the same way.

blocks.example: Let's meet before the call so we're all on the same page.
